question.text: A trader writes (sells) a put option with strike Rs. 17,500 and receives premium Rs. 200. At expiry, the underlying is at Rs. 17,200. What is the writer's profit/loss?

explanation.text: The Logic: Short Put P/L = Premium - max(X - S, 0). With Premium = 200, X = 17,500, S = 17,200: payoff to the buyer = max(17,500 - 17,200, 0) = Rs. 300, so writer's P/L = 200 - 300 = -Rs. 100. Spot 17,200 is below the put writer's BEP of 17,300, so the writer has a loss. The Trap: Profit of Rs. 200 ignores the buyer's payoff and keeps the full premium. Loss of Rs. 300 takes only the buyer's payoff without crediting the premium. Profit of Rs. 300 inverts the loss. Note: Broken comparison after "Spot 17,200" repaired — explanation now reads "spot 17,200 is below the put writer BEP of 17,300, so the writer has a loss."
